page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a constrained-vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The cache subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by standard enterprise instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. A bundled 3780 GB local NVMe SSD provides fast temporary storage without requiring network storage attachments. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded compute and solid memory subsystem execution. The server delivered a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3789.09 and gzip compression throughput of 40.71 GB/sec. PassMark evaluations placed the instance in the top 25 percent across CPU aggregate (58651.77), extended instructions (57914.22), and memory score (2886.79). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 207.89 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-core stress-ng throughput and database operation benchmarks placed within the middle 50 percent, reflecting the constrained 32 vCPU count relative to full-socket equivalents. High-parameter LLM generation on the CPU is limited, registering 2.45 tokens per second for 70B models due to the lack of dedicated tensor acceleration.

The constrained vCPU allocation offers operational cost efficiency for software products licensed on a per-core basis that simultaneously require substantial memory allocations. Bundled high-capacity local NVMe storage reduces external block storage overhead for high-churn intermediate data. Tradeoffs center on lower aggregate parallel throughput compared to unconstrained 64-vCPU counterparts. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise relational database management systems, and large-scale ETL data transformation jobs requiring fast local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 512.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 3780 GB local NVMe SSD, with no discrete GPU accelerators. The 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio yields 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Benchmarks demonstrate upper-tier single-core CPU compute, scoring 3789.09 in stress-ng, along with top-quartile PassMark CPU and memory metrics. While multi-core throughput and large LLM generation reflect the reduced vCPU allocation, its dense memory and fast local NVMe storage deliver strong cost efficiency for core-licensed environments. The server is well aligned for large in-memory caching tiers, enterprise relational databases, big data analytics, and intermediate ETL staging.
